This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/spec`, touching **4** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/src/data/currency-fraction-digits.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

- `content/docs/data-modeling/currency.mdx`  _(via rateField (literal, a string literal in refuseDishonestHomeAmount))_

- `content/docs/releases/v18/18-3.mdx`  _(via rateField (literal, a string literal in refuseDishonestHomeAmount))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/src/data/currency-fraction-digits.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **3** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **63** of **221** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **158** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **158**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **103** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **170** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json af8aab1b1c4f479b9b102da9227279534b4d27cd` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `3cbe1a1fb6f87c73cb6711a28417be8dc1a8ac27` — the merge of head `fcb86f79a42b967c781e8ae92ab9c4e17eeb8c3e` into base `af8aab1b1c4f479b9b102da9227279534b4d27cd`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 3cbe1a1fb6f87c73cb6711a28417be8dc1a8ac27 && git checkout 3cbe1a1fb6f87c73cb6711a28417be8dc1a8ac27
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin af8aab1b1c4f479b9b102da9227279534b4d27cd fcb86f79a42b967c781e8ae92ab9c4e17eeb8c3e && git checkout -B drift-repro af8aab1b1c4f479b9b102da9227279534b4d27cd && git merge --no-ff fcb86f79a42b967c781e8ae92ab9c4e17eeb8c3e

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json af8aab1b1c4f479b9b102da9227279534b4d27cd
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs af8aab1b1c4f479b9b102da9227279534b4d27cd` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **Newly refused — right.** An object whose `record`-mode `currency` amount declares `currencyConfig.homeAmount.rateField` naming a `number` field with a DECLARED `scale` of 0 to 11. One `custom` issue at `fields.AMOUNT.currencyConfig.homeAmount.rateField` naming the field, its `scale`, the floor 12 and the two fixes (object.zod.ts L2171-2184). It runs inside `ObjectSchema`'s superRefine (L3950), so it reaches every door that parses an object: `ObjectStackDefinitionSchema` (`os validate` validate.ts L375, `os compile` compile.ts L442, the lint scorer, scaffold-validate, `os migrate meta` L1232), `EnvironmentArtifactSchema.metadata` (artifact ingest, plugin.ts L1383, a throwing `.parse`), the metadata save door (422), and the registry's registration diagnostic for a stored row (`register` → `validate` → `ObjectSchema.parse`, logged `[metadata_spec_invalid]`, registered anyway; registry.ts L7248). Nothing else is refused: `scale` is read only off the parsed `number` target (`typeof scale === 'number'`), so a non-number `scale` is already `FieldSchema`'s refusal, a non-`number` target is the existing arm above it, and `scale` on the amount or the home field is not read.
2. **Still accepted — right.** `scale` 12 or more; an UNDECLARED `scale` (pinned: `'scale' in BASE_FIELDS.amount_rate` is false and the parse passes); a rate column shared by amounts with the same `currencyField` and `rateDate`, judged once on the first holder (`rateOwner`), so the shared-column pin gets exactly one issue. Accepting an undeclared `scale` needs no new choice: an absent `scale` on a `number` field is already ruled "no fixed width — the value's natural precision" (maintainer ruling 5791809146, field-scale.ts L59-62; `resolveFieldScale` answers `undefined`), so an undeclared rate field shows every digit the column holds. The dev's reading is the platform's own, not a decision taken for the maintainer.
3. **The floor's premise holds against the cited code.** The rate row is `sys_exchange_rate.rate`, `Field.number({ scale: EXCHANGE_RATE_SCALE /* 12 */, precision: EXCHANGE_RATE_PRECISION /* 24 */ })`, the ruling's numbers. The projection stores "the rate row's own value, never rounded" (home-amount-projection.ts L38-44). A rate field is `readonly`, and a readonly value is reached for its SHAPE only — `ReadonlyValueScope` lists `min` / `max` / `scale` / `precision` as the constraints it does NOT reach (record-validator.ts L707-709) — so the declared `scale` constrains no write; the column is `numericColumnFor('number')` = DECIMAL(65,30) on every SQL driver (sql-driver-column-creation.ts L971-981) whatever the field declares. So a `scale` below 12 reaches the display alone and shows a rate that does not reproduce the stored home amount — the exact dishonesty the card names. Refusing it at parse is the right seam; the floor 12 is the ruling's number, not a new one.
4. **Engine and stored data untouched — right.** The diff moves nothing in objectql, platform-objects or driver code; every stored row keeps its digits. (Stored METADATA is another matter: see ④ 3.)
5. **`CURRENCY_FRACTION_DIGITS` TSDoc — right.** The table's values are a CLDR `currencyData` probe (`Intl.NumberFormat(...).resolvedOptions().maximumFractionDigits`, provenance block L44-50), so "CLDR fraction digits, not ISO 4217 minor units" is what the code does. The sixteen codes re-derived here from the table: of its 33 zero-digit entries, 16 carry a non-zero ISO 4217 minor unit (IQD 3; AFN, ALL, COP, HUF, IDR, IRR, KPW, LAK, LBP, MGA, MMK, PKR, SOS, SYP, YER 2) plus SLL, whose ISO entry is withdrawn; every 3-digit entry (BHD, JOD, KWD, LYD, OMR, TND) matches ISO; no 2-digit entry is an ISO 0-, 3- or 4-minor-unit code; XDR and XSU are ISO `N.A.`. The triage's "about seventeen" was SLL. No export, key or value of the table moves.
6. **Public surface.** No new export (`HOME_AMOUNT_RATE_SCALE` is module-private). The new semantic entry enters the generated registry (`gen:migration-registry` runs on build/test; no checked-in registry file) and so `spec-changes.json` and the upgrade guide, both built artifacts — `check:generated` and `Lint & Repo Gates` are green on the head. `content/docs/data-modeling/currency.mdx` says the same sixteen codes; `skills/objectstack-data/rules/field-types.md` L175-178 teaches `rateField` as a readonly `number` with no `scale`, which stays accepted — `Skills-docs: none` is right.

### ② Semver level

`.changeset/30103-home-amount-rate-field-scale-floor.md`: `'@objectstack/spec': minor`, `feat(spec)!:`, `**BREAKING**`, `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`, `Metadata-protocol: narrowed`, a `FROM → TO` with the one-line fix, and one marker `adr-0087: registered home-amount-rate-field-scale-floor` resolving to the entry this diff adds. That is AGENTS.md Post-Task Checklist step 3 to the letter: a value refused that an author could write is `narrowed`; a kind takes `minor` on the package the diff moves (`check-changeset-no-major.mjs` LEVEL axis: `narrowed` beside a `(narrowing)` arm, grading `minor`); a breaking changeset carries its migration and exactly one ADR-0087 disposition, and a FROM → TO body cannot ride `no-migration-prescription` (`check-adr-0087-registration.mjs` R2), so `registered` is the only honest disposition — amendment 6668151276 widened the file surface for exactly that entry. Level: right.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Undeclared `scale` accepted without a maintainer choice** — answered, right (① 2): the meaning of an absent `number` scale is already ruled, and the card asked the dev to "decide and state" it, which the arm's TSDoc (L1965-1968), the refusal text, the changeset and the semantic entry all do.
- **16 codes, not "about 17"** — answered, right (① 5). SLL is withdrawn from the current list, so there is no current ISO minor unit to compare; the TSDoc says so by name.
- **The objectql engine pin at `scale: 4`** (engine-home-amount-projection.test.ts L331) — accepted as is. `boot()` registers through `engine.registry.registerObject`, whose body calls neither `register` nor `validate` (read at the head), so no `ObjectSchema` parse and no `[metadata_spec_invalid]` line; the pin keeps proving the engine-level fact the refusal rests on (a declared scale is no write constraint) for a row stored before this release. Out of this PR's surface; nothing to change.

The lines quoting ruling 5805782503's remedy stay as quoted (AGENTS.md: a quoted ruling is not rewritten); the describes and refusal text are the seat's to correct.
- **`HomeAmountSchema.rateField` `.describe()` does not name the floor** (field.zod.ts L657) — **should-fix**, carrier `domain:spec` seat. The describe is the published JSON-schema sentence an AI author reads before writing the field; today it says "a `number` field declaring `readonly: true`" and nothing about `scale`. One clause ("declaring no `scale`, or `scale: 12` or more") closes it. Outside this PR's `hits`; acceptable as a follow-up, and trivially foldable into this PR.
- **The 12 exists twice, no pin** (`HOME_AMOUNT_RATE_SCALE` object.zod.ts L1969, `EXCHANGE_RATE_SCALE` sys-exchange-rate.object.ts L20) — **should-fix** follow-up. Spec cannot import platform-objects, but platform-objects imports spec: export the floor from `@objectstack/spec/data` and let `sys-exchange-rate.object.test.ts` (which already pins `EXCHANGE_RATE_SCALE` to 12 at L124) pin the two equal, or declare `scale` on the rate row from the spec constant. Both cite ruling 6469382727, so drift is unlikely but unpinned.
- **File surface widened by one entry** — right, recorded in amendment 6668151276 before the report.
- `open_questions: []`, `security_findings: none` — nothing to escalate.

### ④ Design judgment

1. **`packages/spec/src/data/object.zod.ts` — holds.** Judged against ruling 6469382727 and the first consumers (`os validate` / `os compile` through `ObjectStackDefinitionSchema`, artifact ingest, the save door). The arm sits after the target and writer checks and inside the `holder === undefined` branch, so it is judged once per column like the readonly mark; the path is the pointer's; the message names field, declared scale, floor, consequence and both fixes, and carries no tracker number (pinned by the test). Tried to break it: a `scale` on a `formula` or `summary` rate target — refused earlier as non-`number`; a first holder refused as non-`number` with a second sharer — the second gets its own existing refusal, unchanged; a rate field declaring `precision` below 24 — not refused, and rightly: on a readonly field `precision` is no write constraint either and reaches no display, so there is nothing dishonest to refuse; a `scale` above `NUMERIC_COLUMN_SCALE` (30) — the column caps it, display only, out of this card. One wording nit, not a finding: "stores the rate it used with all 12 decimals" reads as if every rate carries twelve; it is the rate row's own value, up to twelve. The changeset uses the same phrase.
2. **`packages/spec/src/data/currency-fraction-digits.ts` — holds.** TSDoc only; the table and its key set are untouched, the new text describes what the probe measures (① 5), and the sixteen codes re-derive from the table. The claim "every other code here equals its ISO 4217 minor unit" rests on the CSV cross-read for XCG (absent from the 2024 List One); the PR body says so. No finding.
3. **`packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/18.home-amount-rate-field-scale-floor.ts` — holds, with one should-fix.** Against `SemanticMigration`: kebab `id`, dotted `surface`, `replacement`, `reason`, `acceptanceCriteria`; no `conversionIds` (right: no D2 conversion, and D3 says a migration that cannot be declarative gets a structured TODO — "NOT mechanically converted: raising the scale or deleting it are both right, and which one is the author's display choice" is that reason); no `relevantWhen` (always listed; the conservative default). This entry's `reason` ends "Stored rows are unaffected; the engine already kept every digit" (true of DATA rows) and its `acceptanceCriteria` covers `objectstack validate` alone. Neither is silent, so this is a **should-fix**: add one sentence per leg to `reason` and the boot-line check to `acceptanceCriteria`, the way the sibling does.
